newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Buenos Aires province says to challenge phone hike.
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires province says to challenge phone hike.

text.p: Argentina's key Buenos Aires province Wednesday said it will challenge a telephone tariff change that resulted in major increases in domestic phone bills.
"Users are starting to receive bills containing big rises," the province's Public Services Minister, Hugo Toledo, said in a statement carried by the state-run Telam news agency.
The arguments behind the tariff changes "lose their meaning when the truth shows that they are hurting more than three million Buenos Aires dwellers," he said.
Toledo said Buenos Aires province would take the case to the central government.
The federal government decreed a tariff change late in January, which significantly lowered long-distance and international rates but boosted the price of local calls.

The two telephone companies, Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom Argentina, lobbied long and hard for the changes and argued they would make no profit from the tariff restructuring. They also said the changes should have no major negative inpact on users.
But local newspapers reported that, in some cases, users ended up having to pay twice as much as before.

The controversial decision to change tariffs met with widespread consumer resistance and was suspended by the courts in February, but the goverment appealed and they went into effect pending a Supreme Court resolution.
